title: Tips to Avoid a Mediocre Physique
summary: Using Omar Isuf's response to comments about his unchanged physique as an example, NH argues that powerlifting-centric advice disguised as hypertrophy advice produces mediocre 'spider' physiques. He lists five mistakes: blaming diminishing returns, strength coping, training like a powerlifter, blaming genetics (torso dominance), and running hypertrophy blocks.
claims: Much YouTube hypertrophy advice is powerlifting-centric: strength training wearing a disguise, and it leads to mediocre physiques
Plateaus after 8-9 years are usually caused by training methodology, not natural limits; many naturals made great progress after changing method and mindset
Blaming diminishing returns is a cope advanced lifters use when progress stalls
Size and strength are different goals; trying to pursue both gives a mediocre amount of each, like a restaurant trying to be best at pizza and sushi
Many lifters are strong without looking it and others look far stronger than they are; strength numbers do not answer questions about physique
You cannot gain size without some strength gain, but the ratio of strength to size depends on what you train for
No natural bodybuilder also holds powerlifting records; if one method gave both, nobody would train specifically for either sport
Strength blocks are not needed for hypertrophy; building the big three first is ego, not muscle growth
Training mostly compound presses builds an already-dominant chest and shoulders and worsens imbalances
The spider physique (big torso, small limbs) is caused by compound-only training that treats isolation as an afterthought
Powerlifters will grind squats to exhaustion but do curls with baby weights or swing heavy dumbbells; isolation needs the same intensity as compounds
Doing 10-12 rep cable curls with 10 reps in reserve stimulates nothing; train isolation lifts to failure
Nobody would expect big legs from 10 easy squat reps at 50% of max; arms are no different
Powerbuilding programs are powerlifting programs with three lazy sets of curls or lateral raises slapped on the end; it's always strength first
Arms and other small 'beach' muscles make the difference in a physique and must be treated as a priority to look like one
Torso dominance is mostly a myth created by years of bench and overhead press; people who only curl and do diamond push-ups end up limb dominant
Power lifters have big chests, trunks, legs and back thickness but little width because they only train their sport's prime movers
A hypertrophy block implies the rest of your training is not for hypertrophy; for a bodybuilder all training is hypertrophy training
Many lifters went into strength not as a calling but because they happened to be good at it (the deadlift kid), then their ego keeps them there
Doing a hypertrophy block for six months is like training tennis ten months and then a table tennis block
YouTubers cutting and bulking the same 20 lb each year create an illusion of progress
Strength progression is only a metric to drive progressive overload (weight, sets or reps), not the end goal
Doing 12 sets of presses a week but only 4 sandbagged isolation sets explains small arms
A powerlifter who benches with 150s but curls only 30s has an imbalance to fix, not bad genetics
Strength gives instant gratification as weight on the bar, so when chasing both it naturally takes over your training
He offered to transform Omar's physique within a year: bigger arms, biceps peaks, triceps sweep, forearms and calves
